approach: Use the authors' repository as the reference implementation, but make the entrypoint Python-only because the sandbox exposes no R runtime and only Python, pip, and git can be executed. For the matched claim C1/C2, the exact target is deterministic: reconstruct the theoretical scatter functionals V1=diag(I2,0) and V2=diag(I2, epsilon*diag(2,0)) with epsilon=20/1000, form V1^+ V2 using a spectral Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse, and report the sorted eigenvalues. The simulation with n=1000 and exactly 20 outliers is generated only as a sample-level sanity check and optional plotting input; the exact 1,1,0,0 result comes from the theoretical matrices and is seed-independent. If Rscript happens to be available, reproduce.py will also invoke the authors' illustrative-example script for artifact generation, but it will never depend on R for results/metrics.json.

files.purpose: Single source of truth for all constants: n=1000, n_outliers=20, p=4, W1, W2, epsilon=0.02, seed, pseudo-inverse rank tolerance, expected eigenvalues, tolerance, and file paths.

Implement the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse GINV computation: spectral decomposition of V1, truncate zero eigenvalues, build V1^+, solve the non-symmetric EVP for V1^+ V2, sort eigenvalues descending, and document the null(V1)-null(V2) limitation.
Generate the Section 2.3 Gaussian mixture with exactly 20 outlier rows out of n=1000 and compute sample scatter matrices for optional sanity checks and plots.
Optional helper implementing the paper's relative SVD rank criteria for C5/C6-compatible diagnostics; not required for the matched C1/C2 metric but documented as an equivalent R-to-Python mapping.
Locate the cloned repository and, only if Rscript exists, invoke the authors' R illustrative-example script; otherwise log that R is unavailable and continue with the Python equivalent for metrics.
Thin orchestration entrypoint: parse --smoke, load config, compute theoretical GINV eigenvalues for C1/C2, optionally run the author R script, run sanity checks, and write results/metrics.json.

config.simulation_mean: zeros(p) (paper model has zero mean / A12)
config.seed: 12345 (A4; fixed seed for optional simulation only)
config.V2_theoretical: diag(W1, epsilon*W2) = diag(1,1,0.04,0) (paper, Sec 2.3 / R5 / A5)
config.ginv_operator: V1^+ V2, with V1^+ computed from spectral decomposition of V1 (R1/R2/A10)
config.pinv_rank_tolerance: 1e-10 * max(eigenvalue_V1) for sample matrices; exact rank 2 for theoretical V1 (A7)
config.tolerance: relative 0.1 for finite target rho=1; absolute 0.1 for zero companion eigenvalues (claim contract)
config.R_optional: true; run only if Rscript is on PATH (R11; blocker documented)

steps: Clone or verify the authors' repository at https://github.com/AuroreAA/ICS_PSD_Replication into ./repo; confirm code/ICS_PSD_illustrative_example.R, code/ICS_PSD_illustrative_example_G.R, code/utilities.R, and renv.lock exist.
Create results/ and results/figures/; keep all generated outputs out of the cloned repository.
Implement src/config.py with the exact constants from the claim contract, especially n=1000, n_outliers=20, p=4, W1=I2, W2=diag(2,0), and epsilon=20/1000.

Implement src/ginv.py: (a) eigendecompose V1 with numpy.linalg.eigh; (b) retain eigenvalues greater than the configured rank tolerance; (c) build V1^+ = U diag(1/lambda_r) U^T; (d) form M = V1^+ @ V2; (e) use numpy.linalg.eig for the non-symmetric EVP; (f) discard numerical imaginary parts smaller than 1e-12 and sort real eigenvalues descending.

Implement src/simulate.py: create an n x p sample with first 980 rows from N(0, diag(W1,0)) and last 20 rows from N(0, diag(W1, 2, 0)); use the fixed seed; assert exactly 20 outliers and shape (1000,4).

Implement src/rank_criteria.py as an optional diagnostic only: compute SVD singular values and relative rank criteria lambda_i/lambda_1 < sqrt(nu), < max(n,p)*nu, and cumulative squared eigenvalues < 0.99; do not use it for the C1/C2 pass/fail.

Implement src/author_runner.py: use shutil.which('Rscript'); if found, run the authors' illustrative-example R script from the repository root and capture stdout/stderr; if not found, record 'R unavailable; Python equivalent used' in the log and continue.

Implement reproduce.py: load config, build theoretical V1 and V2, compute GINV eigenvalues, assert four eigenvalues, assert sorted descending, assert ranks rank(V1)=2 and rank(V2)=3, and compare to expected [1,1,0,0] with the configured C1/C2 tolerances.
In reproduce.py, compute pass_C1 = abs(rho1 - 1.0) <= 0.1 and abs(rho2 - 1.0) <= 0.1; compute pass_C2 = abs(rho3) <= 0.1 and abs(rho4) <= 0.1; overall pass is pass_C1 and pass_C2.

Write results/metrics.json containing claim_id, status, method, V1, V2, V1_pinv, V1_pinv_V2, eigenvalues, expected_eigenvalues, tolerance, pass flags, R_script_status, and the null-space limitation note from Remark 1.
Run the smoke mode first, then the full entrypoint: `python reproduce.py --smoke` followed by `python reproduce.py`.
Open results/metrics.json and verify the computed eigenvalues are numerically [1,1,0,0] (or within machine precision) and that the overall pass flag is true.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`. This constructs only the 4x4 theoretical V1 and V2, prints their shapes, ranks, V1^+ V2 matrix, and eigenvalues, and asserts that the sorted eigenvalues match [1,1,0,0] within 1e-12. It exercises the exact data flow used for C1/C2 without generating the full simulation.
intermediate_checks: Assert V1 shape is (4,4), V2 shape is (4,4), and both are symmetric.
Assert rank(V1) = 2 and rank(V2) = 3 for the theoretical matrices.
Assert V1^+ V2 equals diag(1,1,0,0) up to machine precision.
Assert the four GINV eigenvalues are real up to 1e-12 and sorted in descending order.
Check that the first two eigenvalues are 1 and the last two are 0 within machine precision before applying the 0.1 tolerance.
For the optional simulation, assert the generated sample has shape (1000,4), exactly 20 outlier rows, and no NaN values.
Check that Rscript is either found or explicitly reported as unavailable; the metric must not depend on R.
Confirm metrics.json contains both C1 and C2 companion values, not only a single aggregate number.
budget_plan: Total budget ~15 minutes. Setup and repository inspection: 4 minutes. Implement config, GINV, simulation, and reproduce.py: 4 minutes. Smoke test: 1 minute. Full run and metrics.json inspection: 1 minute. Buffer for environment/JSON checks and optional author R invocation attempt: 5 minutes. The numerical computation itself is under 1 second; the budget is dominated by setup and verification.
